content:
I need to set up a theorem which has the following as an assumption :

There is a function f : Nat → Nat such that f 0 is definitionally / judgmentally equal to 0.

I would be very grateful if someone could suggest how that might be done in Lean.

To put the question in some context, I was trying to formalize the notion of based path induction as described in the book "Homotopy Type Theory", as shown in the image below :

I can postulate the existence of such an ind' by having an axiom, but am stuck on how to assert that ind'(...) and c are definitionally equal.
It's not possible to have that as an assumption
definitional equality has a fairly specific meaning in Lean parlance, and is probably stronger than what you want.
Possibly docs#Eq.subst encodes the property you want from "equality"?

Ruben Van de Velde said:

It's not possible to have that as an assumption

Thanks a lot, I was also beginning to suspect that it might not be possible...

Chris C said:

definitional equality has a fairly specific meaning in Lean parlance, and is probably stronger than what you want.

I don't think Eq.subst is what I want in this case, since it ultimately stems from the type ind'(...) = c being inhabited, which is distinct from ind'(...) and c being judgmentally same. For example, if I don't have judgmental equality, then Eq.refl c : ind'(...) = c wouldn't type check, and I think I would require it further along the way. But still, I'd try giving it a go and see if things work out. Thanks!

fingers crossed! Lean's type theory may not have exactly the same rules as the HoTT book, and in particular it doesn't distinguish between different proofs of the same Prop (including equality) — so you may need to be careful to distinguish Lean itself from the theory you're formalising

@Chris C Yes, I am trying to be careful about carrying things over from HoTT to Lean, this is the code I have going on so far... I am mainly trying to understand for myself how identity types behave, and writing down whatever I understand.
